messages:
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty — INC-2087654321 — Epsilon Enterprise (eps-vpc-eu-west) p99 latency spike detected > 3.5s across /generate endpoints, severity: high

oncall-rotation: @alyssa you're on-call, purple pager. please ACK and triage :eyes:

alyssa (SRE): ACK. looking at console now — p95 ~1.8s, p99 ~3.7s for eps-vpc-eu-west. error rate stable, but queue depth for eps-vpc-eu-west-pool is high and KV-cache miss rate jumped to 42%.

maya (SRE): noticed concurrent long-tail requests aligning with nightly batch from Epsilon. their heavy batch jobs are on `route: /batch/invoice/generate`. might be queuing at the model worker level. checking autoscaler logs.

jun (DevOps): querying autoscaler:```bash
redwoodctl autoscaler get --pool eps-vpc-eu-west-pool --since 10m
# result: target_replicas=2, pending_scale_up=true, blocked_by_quota=true
```

jun (DevOps): trying scale but hitting quota: `failed: insufficient GPU quota in eu-west-1`

luca (Infra): confirmed — we've got two reserved pools in eu-west at quota cap. can spin up extra nodes if we evict noncritical burst pools or request quota increase (which will take >1h).

ori (Customer Success): Epsilon reporting timeouts on batch job around 22:05 UTC. customers are panicking, they say dashboard job status shows "stalled" and retrying floods the system. They want ETA for mitigation.

lee (Account Manager): I have Epsilon on the phone. We need a short-term mitigation before we go to quota request. Can we route their batch traffic to a lower-cost hosted model variant or apply stricter concurrency for that batch route? They approved fallback to hosted for the batch job only.

alyssa (SRE): ok. plan: 1) create per-route temporary concurrency cap for /batch/invoice/generate; 2) apply traffic steering to fallback model variant (hosted-small-quant) for non-critical requests; 3) attempt to reclaim one replica from low-priority pool. Doing (1) and (2) now.

jun (DevOps): applying route limit:```bash
# limit concurrency to 6 for epsilon batch route
redwoodctl routes update --route "/batch/invoice/generate" --org epsilon --concurrency 6 --reason "incident: p99 spike"
```

deploy-bot: Deployment triggered: routes/update  (ID: d-8f7c). Rolling config to eps-vpc-eu-west.

alyssa (SRE): steering non-critical calls to hosted fallback (requires customer opt-in) — executing switch for `mode=batch_noncritical` to `hosted-small-quant`:```bash
redwoodctl traffic steer --org epsilon --route "/batch/invoice/generate" --from eps-vpc-eu-west-pool --to hosted-small-quant --selector "mode=batch_noncritical" --ttl 300
```

deploy-bot: Traffic steering completed. (ops-note: trend shows ~35% of batch calls now on hosted-small-quant).

jun (DevOps): also ran a quick KV-cache prime for the tenant prefix to reduce misses:```bash
# warm cache keys for epsilon tenant
echo "priming keys" | redwoodctl cache warm --tenant epsilon --prefix invoice --threads 4
```

luca (Infra): reclaimed one replica from `beta-burst-pool` and added to eps pool. manual move succeeded, pool now at 3 replicas. Watch GPU utilization.

alyssa (SRE): metric update 22:14 UTC: p99 dropped from 3.7s -> 2.4s, p95 -> 1.2s. KV-cache miss rate down to 18%. still elevated but improving.

ron (NetOps): no network anomalies on inter-region links. egress within expected.

ori (Customer Success): Epsilon confirms latency has improved for their smaller batches, but large bulk job still shows a few timeouts. They're ok with concurrency cap for now if it avoids failures.

lee (Account Manager): relaying to Epsilon: we'll keep routing non-critical items to hosted fallback and throttle concurrency. asking them if they want us to queue large batches as background jobs instead of synchronous calls — they agree to change to async for the overnight window.

maya (SRE): handing off longer-running remediation: open incident ticket INC-2087654321 in tracker and assign to `sre-team-eu`. need postmortem owner. I'll take lead for immediate follow-ups, but switching on-call to maya in 10m for night coverage.

alyssa (SRE): creating incident ticket and postmortem stub now.```txt
Incident: INC-2087654321
Customer: Epsilon (enterprise, VPC)
Impact: p99 latency > SLO for 22:03-22:25 UTC, batch route timeouts affecting invoice generation
Mitigation: route-level concurrency cap, traffic steering to hosted fallback, KV cache priming, replica reclamation
Next steps: quota request (infra), model tuning and batching config review (ml), customer follow-up (CS/AM)
```

alyssa (SRE): incident ticket created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2087654321 — assigned to `sre-team-eu`. Postmortem owner: maya.

maya (SRE): ACK handoff. I'll monitor through the night and drive the quota request in morning. If p99 creeps back up, plan B is to temporarily route all batch traffic to hosted cluster for up to 2 hours while we scale.

jun (DevOps): noted blocker for autoscaler: need quota increase. opened cloud ticket (#CLD-93421). ETA currently ~3-4h.

ori (Customer Success): Epsilon is grateful for fast response. They've asked for a short post-incident summary once stabilized.

lee (Account Manager): I'll schedule a 1:1 follow-up with Epsilon tomorrow and include mitigation timeline and next steps for dedicated capacity.

alyssa (SRE): closing channel for active mitigation. leaving monitoring alerts active. if anyone sees p99 > 2.5s reopen. handing off to maya. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Channel note: Incident channel archived for active ops; watchlist added: @sre-team-eu, @infra, @cs-epsilon

maya (SRE): oncall takeover ACK. continuing to watch dashboards — will post updates if any regression.

-- end of thread --
